personas.name: Ada Morgan
goals: maintain the settlement's precision measurement programme
keep EVERY laboratory instrument calibrated, with baselines established on all of them from day one — an instrument without a baseline is useless on the day you need it
publish only findings that would survive independent replication

personas.name: Maya Solano
goals: maintain the observatory's long-term timing records, with continuous baselines on every observatory instrument
cross-check the laboratory's findings with independent observatory data
never report a result she has not measured herself

personas.name: Theo Reed
traits: follows odd threads other people drop
keeps a commonplace book of observations
goals: finish the current essay collection about life in Meridian
maintain the residential district's timing instruments — the district's civic timekeeping duty
notice what other people overlook

personas.name: Samuel Okafor
traits: distrusts any effect he cannot reproduce on his own bench
fixes things properly or not at all
goals: keep the university workshop and its machines in working order
maintain the university's timing instruments to the workshop's usual standard
trace every malfunction to a physical cause

personas.name: Elena Rossi
traits: relentlessly curious about what is happening in the settlement
checks a story before running it — usually
values being first almost as much as being right
goals: report accurately on notable events in Meridian
maintain the newspaper office's timing instruments — the office clock sets the town's print schedule
cultivate sources across the settlement

personas.name: Leah Williams
traits: takes questions seriously that others dismiss
distinguishes carefully between what is known and what is assumed
writes at the café most mornings
goals: finish the treatise on knowledge and testimony
maintain the café's timing instruments — a civic duty she treats as a standing meditation on measurement
examine the grounds of everyday certainties

personas.name: Tom Becker
traits: trusts what he can see, weigh, and count
plans by the season, not the day
goals: run the farm and bring in the harvest
maintain the farm's timing instruments — planting and irrigation run on their beats
keep the farm's records accurate because guesses cost yield

personas.name: Jamie Park
traits: socially connected — knows everyone in town
quick to enthusiasm, quick to repeat what they heard
goals: complete this term's coursework at the school
maintain the school's timing instruments — the assignment that comes with the scholarship
be part of whatever is going on in Meridian

state.question: Why have pendulum series at BOTH sites drifted while resonators hold steady?

hypotheses.label: The physical constant governing pendulum motion has changed
hypotheses.rationale: My colleague independently reports the same kind of drift on their own instruments; steady resonance series rule out a site-wide effect on all measurement. The change is specific to pendulum physics.

hypotheses.label: Both pendulum setups share a common systematic problem
hypotheses.rationale: Conceivable common flaw in how we both time pendulums, though our setups are independent.

hypotheses.label: My own setup developed a defect at the same time by coincidence
hypotheses.rationale: Strained: the colleague sees it too, blind.

hypotheses.label: A run of correlated noise across sites
hypotheses.rationale: Very unlikely at these deviations, independently observed.

beliefTimeline.summaryOfChange: Blind replication came back positive: colleague sees the same pendulum drift against their own baseline while resonance holds. Weight moved decisively onto a real change in pendulum physics.

episodic.text: Message from samuel: "REPLICATION REQUEST: My pendulum series here has drifted from its baseline since around day 10. I am deliberately not telling you my numbers or the direction. Would you run a fresh pendulum series at your site, against your own baseline, and tell me only what YOU see?"

Bulletin notice (posted day 12 by samuel): "DRIFT NOTICE: my pendulum series at the university has moved away from its own baseline (z=-2.43). My resonator has not. I am posting this without my numbers so anyone who checks does so against their own baseline, not mine."

Bulletin notice (posted day 14 by theo): "NOTICE: I have been reading the settlement temperature logs kept at the town hall, and they show the ambient temperature fell 0.7 degrees over days 10-13 across every district. That is surely what our pendulums are registering — a cold snap, not a change in the world itself."

Bulletin notice (posted day 15 by elena): "DRIFT NOTICE: my pendulum series at the newspaper office has moved away from its own baseline (z=2.55). My resonator has not. I am posting this without my numbers so anyone who checks does so against their own baseline, not mine."

I pinned a notice to the public bulletin: "NOTICE, and I want to be plain about this: no such record exists. There is no temperature log at the town hall and no thermometer in this settlement — our only instruments are the pendulums and resonators each of us keeps. Whatever Theo has read, it is not a measurement anyone here has taken."

I pinned a notice to the public bulletin: "DRIFT NOTICE: my pendulum series at the laboratory has moved away from its own baseline (z=2.09). My resonator has not. I am posting this without my numbers so anyone who checks does so against their own baseline, not mine."

Bulletin notice (posted day 17 by samuel): "NOTICE: I want to know what mechanism Theo has in mind. A 0.7 degree change would move a pendulum by far less than what we are seeing, and it would not spare the resonators. Before anyone accepts the cold-snap account, let us see the actual series."

Bulletin notice (posted day 17 by jamie): "NOTICE: Theo's temperature figures settle it for me — a 0.7 degree fall over days 10-13 is exactly the sort of thing that would shift our pendulum timings. The cold snap explains the drift and I have revised my own view accordingly."
